meta.document_title: CasAlerts — Scaling to 100,000 Users: Engineering Devguide
meta.status: Living document — update as items are completed
meta.purpose: Comprehensive engineering checklist to scale CasAlerts from current pre-launch state to reliably serving 100,000 users without data loss, missed alerts, or user-visible degradation.

priority_key.P0: Breaks before 10k users. MUST be done before any marketing push.
priority_key.P1: Breaks between 10k and 50k users. MUST be done within 60 days post-launch growth.
priority_key.P2: Required to reach 100k users cleanly. Do before crossing 30k.
priority_key.P3: Polish / cost optimization. Do after the above.

critical_data_rules: NEVER remove or modify existing data collection code without explicit instruction.
Every new feature must log appropriate compliance_events and analytics_events.
Every violation insertion must include severity_classification.
Every property enrichment must save zip_code, latitude, longitude, parcel_id where available.
Resolution data (costs, contractors, ratings) is the most valuable proprietary data — never lose it.
The violation_external_id must be saved in violation_resolutions to survive rescans.
meta.current_architecture_failure_point: Current sequential CRON loop will fail at ~2,000-3,000 properties (Vercel 300s timeout). Must be fixed before any real growth.

categories.title: Background Processing & CRON Architecture
categories.summary: The single most critical area. Current in-process CRON loop will fail before 3k properties. All alert delivery, scoring, and scanning must move to a queue-based architecture with retries, idempotency, and dead-letter queues.

items.title: Replace in-process CRON loop with a queue (Inngest or QStash)
items.problem: app/api/cron/scan-violations/route.ts iterates every property sequentially in a single Vercel function invocation. At 210k properties x ~2s per property = ~117 hours. Vercel Pro caps function duration at 300s. Current code will be silently truncated — some properties get scanned, some do not, with no visibility into which. This is a data-integrity disaster since your moat depends on collecting every data point correctly.
solution_steps: Adopt Inngest (recommended — Next.js native, typed events, generous free tier) or QStash (simpler, HTTP-based).
Split the monolithic CRON into four phases, each dispatched as events: scan.property.requested, alert.new_violation.send, alert.reminder.send, score.snapshot.requested.
Dispatcher CRON runs daily, queries all properties, enqueues one event per property, then returns immediately (<5s).
Each worker handler must be idempotent and use onFailure retry with exponential backoff (3 retries: 30s, 2min, 10min).
Concurrency limit per worker: 10 (respects Socrata/Carto rate limits — see external-api category).
Keep maxDuration=60 on the dispatcher route. Individual workers get 300s each on Vercel Pro.
Log every event enqueue + dequeue to cron_runs table for observability.
files_affected: MODIFY: app/api/cron/scan-violations/route.ts — becomes a thin dispatcher that enqueues events, removes the loop body
MODIFY: vercel.json — no crons config change, but verify maxDuration=60 on dispatcher
verification: Trigger dispatcher manually via curl with CRON_SECRET — confirm N events enqueued where N = count of properties.
Simulate a failing property (throw in worker) — confirm it retries 3 times, then lands in Inngest DLQ (not silently lost).
Time full end-to-end run — target <30 min for 210k properties at concurrency 10.
Check cron_runs table — every property should have exactly one successful scan row per day.
items.do_not_change: Do NOT remove any existing violation insertion logic, severity classification, or compliance_event logging. Only change WHERE it runs (worker vs inline loop).

items.title: Dead-letter queue for failed email/SMS alerts
items.problem: Today, if Resend or Twilio fails, the error is logged to console and forgotten. needs_alert is still cleared in the database. The user never gets the alert. This silently breaks the core product promise at scale where transient provider errors become common.
solution_steps: Create failed_alerts table with idempotency key, retry count, next_retry_at.
In lib/email-alerts.ts and lib/sms-alerts.ts: on failure, do NOT clear needs_alert — insert into failed_alerts instead.
Add retry worker (lib/inngest/functions/retry-failed-alerts.ts) running every 15 minutes via Inngest cron trigger.
Retry logic: exponential backoff 5min, 15min, 1h, 6h, 24h. After 5 failed attempts mark as error_permanent and fire a Sentry alert.
Add admin dashboard route app/admin/failed-alerts/page.tsx to view and manually re-trigger.
On successful retry, fire compliance_event: alert_delivered_after_retry for moat data.
files_affected: MODIFY: lib/email-alerts.ts — on error, insert into failed_alerts table
MODIFY: lib/sms-alerts.ts — on error, insert into failed_alerts table
MODIFY: app/api/cron/scan-violations/route.ts — do NOT clear needs_alert if send failed
items.sql:
create table failed_alerts (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  channel text not null check (channel in ('email','sms')),
  recipient text not null,
  user_id uuid references profiles(id) on delete cascade,
  property_id uuid references properties(id) on delete cascade,
  violation_id uuid references violations(id) on delete set null,
  idempotency_key text not null,
  payload jsonb not null,
  error_message text,
  attempt_count int not null default 1,
  next_retry_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  resolved_at timestamptz,
  resolution_type text check (resolution_type in ('delivered','error_permanent','manual_cancel')),
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
create index idx_failed_alerts_retry on failed_alerts(next_retry_at) where resolved_at is null;
create index idx_failed_alerts_user on failed_alerts(user_id, created_at desc);
verification: Simulate Resend outage (invalid API key in staging) — confirm failed_alerts row appears AND needs_alert stays true on the violation.
Restore API key, wait for retry worker — confirm row marked resolved and user receives email.
Verify that a single failed alert cannot be duplicate-retried (idempotency_key unique check).
items.do_not_change: Do not change the compliance_event logging in email/SMS send functions. Preserve all existing success-path data collection.

items.title: Idempotency keys on every outbound alert
items.problem: At scale with retries (from bg-01 and bg-02), duplicate emails/SMS become statistically certain. A landlord receiving the same alert 3 times erodes trust instantly and wastes $$ on SMS.
solution_steps: Compute idempotency key in lib/alert-idempotency.ts: sha256(violation_id + channel + user_id) for new-violation alerts; sha256(reminder_id + channel + scheduled_date) for reminders.
Create alert_sends table with idempotency_key as PRIMARY KEY.

Before sending in sendNewViolationEmail/sendNewViolationSMS/sendReminder*: insert into alert_sends with 'on conflict do nothing'. If 0 rows inserted, the send already happened — return {success:true, skipped:true} without calling Resend/Twilio.
After successful send, UPDATE alert_sends.external_id with provider message ID for auditing.
Document idempotency boundary: an idempotency window of 7 days is appropriate (reminders may legitimately re-send after that).
verification: Unit test: call sendNewViolationEmail twice with same payload — confirm second call returns skipped=true and only one Resend call fires.
Integration test: trigger Inngest retry on a successful send — confirm no duplicate.
Check alert_sends row count equals actual delivery count for a test run.
items.do_not_change: Preserve all compliance_event logging on successful sends.

items.title: Per-property scan observability (cron_runs table)
items.problem: Without per-property timing, you cannot identify which addresses (many violations, slow geocoding, flaky city APIs) are blowing up your CRON budget. You also cannot tell if CRON ran successfully today at all.
solution_steps: Create cron_runs table.
Wrap each worker handler: const start = Date.now(); try { ... } finally { insert cron_runs(duration_ms: Date.now()-start, ok, phase, property_id) }.
Create materialized view cron_health_daily (rolled up per day + phase).
Alert via Sentry if any phase's p95 exceeds 5s over a run — indicates city API slowdown.
Alert if any property has 3 consecutive failed scans — likely bad address or deleted from city DB.
files_affected: MODIFY: all lib/inngest/functions/*.ts — wrap handlers with timing
verification: After one CRON run, query: select phase, count(*), percentile_cont(0.95) within group (order by duration_ms) from cron_runs where run_date = current_date group by phase.
Confirm row count for phase='scan' equals total property count.

items.title: CRON health check endpoint with alerting
items.problem: If CRON silently stops running (Vercel config change, env var issue, expired secret), users stop receiving alerts and you find out from an angry email. Unacceptable at 100k users.
solution_steps: Create app/api/health/cron/route.ts that queries cron_runs: returns 200 if last successful scan within last 25 hours, 500 otherwise.
Register endpoint with UptimeRobot or BetterStack — ping every 5 minutes.
Configure notification to email + SMS + Slack on failure.
Add a secondary anomaly check: if total alerts sent today < 50% of 7-day moving average, alert. Prevents silent 'CRON ran but produced no output' bugs.
verification: Temporarily disable CRON — confirm UptimeRobot alerts within 30 minutes.
Seed anomalous data (only 1 alert today) — confirm anomaly endpoint returns 500.

items.title: Daily digest mode for alerts (reduce notification fatigue and cost)
items.problem: At 100k users, per-violation alerts flood users (and your Resend/Twilio bill). A landlord with 50 properties gets 30 separate emails if CRON finds 30 new violations. They unsubscribe. You also pay per email.
solution_steps: Add profiles.alert_mode column: 'realtime' (default for backward compat) or 'daily_digest'.
In daily_digest mode: CRON inserts violations with needs_alert=true, but send worker batches by user_id and sends ONE email per user per day listing all new violations across all properties.
Add settings UI toggle at app/settings — default new signups to daily_digest after launch.
SMS remains realtime for critical severity only (paid tier).
Track: compliance_event type='digest_sent' with counts for moat data.
items.sql: alter table profiles add column if not exists alert_mode text not null default 'realtime' check (alert_mode in ('realtime','daily_digest'));
verification: Enable digest mode for a test user with 5 properties. Seed 10 new violations. Confirm exactly 1 email sent with all 10 listed.
Confirm realtime users still get per-property emails (no regression).

categories.title: Database Schema, Indexes & Partitioning
categories.summary: Without these changes, every dashboard query degrades as data grows. Partitioning is required for analytics_events and score history tables that will reach 100M+ rows.

items.title: Add all missing indexes on hot query paths
items.problem: Multiple queries in app/dashboard/page.tsx, app/dashboard/[propertyId]/page.tsx, and cron-scan-violations.ts filter on columns without indexes. At 10M violation rows, these become full table scans. Dashboard TTFB would climb to 10+ seconds.
solution_steps: Run all index statements in a single migration.
Use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in production to avoid table locks.
Run VACUUM ANALYZE after to update planner stats.
Verify with EXPLAIN ANALYZE on each query.
verification: Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on every SELECT in dashboard-page.tsx — must show Index Scan, never Seq Scan.
Seed 100k violations in staging. Dashboard load time should be <500ms p95.
After migration, run: select schemaname, indexrelname, idx_scan from pg_stat_user_indexes order by idx_scan desc; — confirm new indexes are being used.

items.title: Partition analytics_events, compliance_score_history, compliance_events by month
items.problem: analytics_events grows ~100M rows/year, compliance_score_history grows 76M/year, compliance_events grows ~20M/year. Without partitioning, every query against these tables slows linearly with size, and VACUUM becomes painful. Index bloat degrades writes too.
solution_steps: Convert each table to partitioned via this pattern: create _new as partitioned, copy data in batches, rename old to _old, rename _new to original name.
Create next 3 months of partitions up-front.
Add monthly CRON job (lib/inngest/functions/rotate-partitions.ts) that creates next month's partition and drops old partitions per retention policy.

Retention policies: analytics_events 180 days (move to cold storage after); compliance_score_history 2 years (aggregate older to monthly avg); compliance_events keep forever but move >2yr to cold storage.
Use partman extension if available in Supabase (it is) — simplifies partition management dramatically.
verification: Run explain on: select * from analytics_events where user_id = X and created_at > now() - interval '7 days'; — confirm partition pruning (only 1-2 child partitions scanned).
Verify row count matches pre-migration count exactly.
Run rotate-partitions CRON in staging, confirm next month's partition created.
Confirm all writes still succeed after swap.
items.caution: This is a disruptive migration. Do it during low-traffic window. Have rollback plan: keep _old table for 2 weeks before dropping.

items.title: Populate property_stats table — kill the dashboard N+1
items.problem: app/dashboard/page.tsx for a Pro user with 50 properties runs 6+ queries, each fetching ALL data for ALL their properties, then aggregating in JS. At 100k users this melts the DB. The property_stats table already exists but is not being populated — this is low-hanging fruit with massive impact.
solution_steps: Add missing columns to property_stats (see SQL).
Create lib/property-stats.ts with recomputePropertyStats(propertyId) that reads violations/resolutions/reminders, computes all metrics, upserts into property_stats.
Emit Inngest event property.stats.recompute.requested from: end of CRON scan, after resolution submission, after reminder created/cleared, after property onboarding, after property removed.
Rewrite app/dashboard/page.tsx: single query joins properties + property_stats. Remove all in-JS aggregation loops.
Keep DashboardContent.tsx filters working — filter on the single joined result set.
Add freshness fallback: if property_stats.updated_at < now() - 10 minutes, fire recompute event (background) and use stale data for this render.
files_affected: MODIFY: app/dashboard/page.tsx — strip all aggregation loops, single join on property_stats
MODIFY: app/dashboard/DashboardContent.tsx — consume stats as props, no client-side computation
MODIFY: app/dashboard/[propertyId]/actions.ts — emit event after resolution/reminder actions
MODIFY: app/api/cron/scan-violations/route.ts — emit event per scanned property
MODIFY: app/onboarding/actions.ts — emit event after property creation
MODIFY: app/dashboard/actions.ts — emit event after property removal (to clean up stats row)
items.sql:
alter table property_stats
  add column if not exists open_violations_count int not null default 0,
  add column if not exists complaint_count int not null default 0,
  add column if not exists pending_verification_count int not null default 0,
  add column if not exists resolved_count int not null default 0,
  add column if not exists spend_min numeric not null default 0,
  add column if not exists spend_max numeric not null default 0,
  add column if not exists current_score int check (current_score is null or (current_score between 0 and 100)),
  add column if not exists current_grade text,
  add column if not exists grade_color text,
  add column if not exists overdue_count int not null default 0,
  add column if not exists critical_count int not null default 0,
  add column if not exists high_count int not null default 0,
  add column if not exists moderate_count int not null default 0,
  add column if not exists low_count int not null default 0,
  add column if not exists admin_count int not null default 0,
  add column if not exists updated_at timestamptz not null default now();
create unique index if not exists ux_property_stats_property on property_stats(property_id);
create index if not exists idx_property_stats_user on property_stats(user_id);
verification: Load dashboard with a test account having 100 properties — confirm in Supabase query log: <3 queries against violations or violation_resolutions total.
Page TTFB drops from seconds to <200ms.
Resolve a violation, wait 5s, refresh dashboard — confirm stats updated.
Add a new violation via CRON — confirm stats row updated.
items.do_not_change: Do NOT change the compliance score calculation logic in lib/compliance-score.ts. Only change WHERE the score is computed (background vs request-time). The exact same inputs and outputs must be preserved.

items.title: Database-level data integrity constraints
items.problem: Code-level checks can be bypassed by bugs, migrations, or manual SQL. Your moat depends on severity_classification being always set and violation_external_id being always preserved. Defense in depth via database constraints is free insurance.
solution_steps: Run all constraint additions in one migration.
Before adding NOT NULL constraints, run a data fix pass to handle existing nulls (backfill to 'moderate' for severity).
Add CHECK constraints with reasonable bounds.
verification: Attempt manual insert of violation with null severity — must fail with constraint violation.
Attempt insert of resolution with negative cost — must fail.
Attempt duplicate violation (same external_id + property_id) — must fail.
Run full CRON — confirm no constraint violations in logs.

items.title: Supabase compute upgrade path
items.problem: Default Pro plan ships with Micro compute (1GB RAM, shared vCPU). This handles ~50 concurrent users. At 1500 peak sessions, database becomes bottleneck.
solution_steps: At ~500 users: upgrade to Small ($15/mo add-on).
At ~5000 users: upgrade to Medium ($60/mo).
At ~20000 users: upgrade to Large ($110/mo).
At ~50000 users: upgrade to XL ($210/mo) or consider read replicas (db-06).
Monitor Supabase Dashboard > Reports > Database > CPU + Connection Pool saturation.
Set Supabase Database Alerts: CPU >70% for 10 min, connection pool >80%.
verification: After each upgrade, verify p95 query latency drops in Supabase Advisors tab.
Monitor for 48h post-upgrade to ensure no regression.

items.title: Read replicas for reporting and admin queries
items.problem: Admin dashboards, internal analytics, and heavy reporting queries compete with user-facing traffic. At 50k+ users this causes lock contention on primary.
solution_steps: Enable Supabase Read Replica (available on Pro plan $50/mo per replica).
Create lib/supabase/readreplica.ts client pointing at replica endpoint.
Route admin pages, analytics queries, and reporting to replica.
Keep writes + user-facing reads on primary.
Accept eventual consistency (typically <1s lag).
files_affected: MODIFY: app/admin/**/*.tsx to use readreplica client
verification: Load admin dashboard — confirm queries hit replica (monitor in Supabase logs).
Write new violation — confirm user dashboard (on primary) shows it immediately.

items.title: Connection pooling via PgBouncer / Supavisor
items.problem: Serverless functions open new connections on every invocation. At high concurrency, you exhaust Postgres max_connections (default 100 on Small compute).
solution_steps: Use Supabase Supavisor transaction-mode pooler URL for all serverless routes. Port 6543.
Reserve session-mode pooler (port 5432) only for migrations and long-running queries.
Update NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL or a separate SUPABASE_POOLED_URL env var.
Verify in lib/supabase/server.ts and lib/supabase/admin.ts that all clients use the pooled connection.
Use prepared-statement-free queries (Supabase JS client already does this correctly in transaction mode).
files_affected: MODIFY: .env.local + Vercel env vars — add SUPABASE_DB_POOLER_URL
verification: Monitor Supabase > Reports > Connection Pool — should stay <50% under load.
Load test with k6 at 1000 concurrent requests — no 'too many connections' errors.

items.title: Autovacuum tuning for high-churn tables
items.problem: violations, analytics_events, and compliance_events get many UPDATEs (status changes) and INSERTs. Default autovacuum thresholds (20% dead tuples) are too lax for write-heavy tables at scale. Bloat degrades queries.
solution_steps: Set per-table autovacuum settings: scale_factor 0.05, analyze_scale_factor 0.02.
Schedule weekly VACUUM ANALYZE on hot tables (via Supabase SQL Editor or Inngest cron).
Monitor pg_stat_user_tables.n_dead_tup — alert if > 100k on any table.
verification: After a week, query pg_stat_user_tables — dead_tup ratio should stay <10% on these tables.

categories.title: Caching & Query Optimization
categories.summary: Move hot reads off the database. Introduce pagination and caching layers.

items.title: Add Upstash Redis for hot-path caching
items.problem: Dashboard and property detail pages re-fetch identical data for the same user across page navigations. Compliance scores and property_stats rarely change between CRON runs. Free-tier users hitting the same endpoints repeatedly generate unnecessary DB load.
solution_steps: Add @upstash/redis. Free tier: 10k commands/day, enough for <2k users; paid $10/mo for 100k req/day.
Cache keys with TTLs: property_stats:{propertyId} 5min, compliance_score:{propertyId} 30min, city:list 1h, user_profile:{userId} 5min.
Invalidate on write: after resolution submit, property_stats recompute, profile update.
Use Redis for rate limiting too (see sec-01).
Never cache PII-heavy data or cross-user data — cache keys must be user-scoped.
files_affected: NEW: lib/cache.ts (get/set/invalidate helpers with typed keys)
MODIFY: app/dashboard/page.tsx — wrap property_stats fetch with cache.getOrSet
MODIFY: lib/property-stats.ts — invalidate cache after recompute
verification: First dashboard load hits DB; second load within 5min hits Redis (0 DB queries on property_stats).
Resolve a violation — confirm cache invalidated and next load shows updated score.

items.title: Paginate violations history on property detail
items.problem: Properties with 100+ violations load everything at once in app/dashboard/[propertyId]/page.tsx. Slow render, huge payload, poor mobile UX.
solution_steps: Default load: 25 most recent violations.
Add Load More button (server action or client pagination).
Keep 'open' violations always visible (show open list separately with all of them).
Use React Suspense to stream initial view while history loads.
verification: Seed property with 500 violations — initial load shows 25 + open. Load More fetches next 25.

items.title: Denormalize city_slug onto properties table
items.problem: Every dashboard query joins properties → cities for slug lookup. Tiny cost individually, meaningful at scale.
solution_steps: Add properties.city_slug column.
Backfill from join.
Update onboarding/actions.ts to write city_slug on insert.
Update all queries to use properties.city_slug directly.
files_affected: MODIFY: all queries that currently join cities
verification: EXPLAIN dashboard query — confirm no cities join.
Onboard new property — confirm city_slug populated.

items.title: Cache city API enrichment responses (Cook County / OPA)
items.problem: Property enrichment from Cook County and OPA is slow (30s timeout) and these APIs have rate limits. Re-enriching or onboarding the same property twice within a day hits the API redundantly.
solution_steps: Add property_details.last_enriched_at timestamp.
Before calling city API, check: if last_enriched_at > now() - 7 days, skip API call and use existing.
User can force re-enrich via button (bypasses cache).
Fallback: if API times out, use cached value if available and log a compliance_event enrichment_fallback_used.
items.sql: alter table property_details add column if not exists last_enriched_at timestamptz;
verification: Onboard same address twice in 5 minutes — second should skip API call (check cron_runs for 'enrichment' phase count).

categories.title: External API Resilience (Socrata, Carto, Cook County, OPA, Resend, Twilio, Stripe)
categories.summary: At 210k properties scanned daily you will hit rate limits, transient failures, and outages constantly. Without retry + circuit breaker + fallback, each becomes a user-facing bug.

items.title: Register + rotate Socrata app tokens, enforce rate limits
items.problem: Chicago Socrata unauthenticated limit is ~1000 req/hour shared. With app token: 50k/hour per token. At 150k Chicago properties + rescans + address searches, you need tokens and pacing. Current code has one token — no fallback if rate-limited.
solution_steps: Register 3 app tokens at data.cityofchicago.org (free).
Store as SOCRATA_APP_TOKEN_1, _2, _3 env vars.
Create lib/socrata-client.ts that round-robins tokens.
On 429 response, rotate to next token + exponential backoff.
Centralize all Socrata calls through this client (currently scattered).
Cap concurrency at 10 simultaneous Socrata requests globally (use Inngest throttle or Redis semaphore).
verification: Monitor token usage at data.cityofchicago.org admin.
Simulate 429 — confirm retry with different token succeeds.
Under sustained load, zero 429s should reach user.

items.title: Carto SQL API retry + backoff wrapper
items.problem: Philadelphia Carto API has transient 500s and sometimes returns empty responses when overloaded. No current retry logic — first failure = missed data.
solution_steps: Create lib/carto-client.ts with retry (3 attempts, 1s/3s/10s backoff).
On transient failure (5xx, timeout, empty response when rows expected): retry.
On permanent failure (4xx, bad query): do not retry, log error.
Cap concurrency at 5 simultaneous Carto requests.
verification: Simulate 503 response — confirm 3 retries before giving up.
Confirm successful retries are transparent to caller.

items.title: Circuit breaker for Cook County Assessor
items.problem: Cook County API is known to be slow + unreliable. When it is down, every enrichment attempt blocks 30s and degrades onboarding UX.
solution_steps: Implement circuit breaker (lib/circuit-breaker.ts): after 5 consecutive failures or >50% error rate over 20 requests, open circuit for 5 minutes.
While open, skip API call and use whatever data we have (don't block user).
Log compliance_event enrichment_skipped_circuit_open for moat data.
Re-enrich queue: when circuit closes, enqueue missing enrichments to run later.
files_affected: MODIFY: lib/property-enrichment.ts — Cook County call wrapped in circuit breaker
verification: Simulate Cook County outage — onboarding should still complete (property created with basic data, enrichment deferred).
Confirm enrichment retried when circuit closes.

items.title: Resend webhook handler (bounces, complaints, unsubscribes)
items.problem: When emails bounce or users mark as spam, Resend tells you via webhook. Currently no handler — your sender reputation degrades invisibly, and you keep sending to invalid addresses (waste + eventual block).
solution_steps: Create app/api/webhooks/resend/route.ts. Verify signature with RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
Handle events: email.bounced, email.complained, email.delivery_delayed.
On bounce: mark profile.email_bounced=true and stop sending (log compliance_event).
On complaint (marked as spam): mark profile.email_suppressed=true and unsubscribe ALL channels.
Add email_suppressions table for audit trail.
Register webhook URL in Resend dashboard.
files_affected: MODIFY: lib/email-alerts.ts — check suppression before sending
verification: Use Resend test bounce — confirm webhook fires, profile marked, future sends to that email skipped.
Verify webhook signature — reject unsigned requests with 401.

items.title: Twilio webhook + STOP/HELP handling (legally required)
items.problem: US SMS regulations (CTIA) REQUIRE that users can text STOP to unsubscribe. If you don't handle this you can be fined and Twilio will suspend your account.
solution_steps: Create app/api/webhooks/twilio/route.ts for inbound SMS.
Parse body: if STOP → mark profile.sms_suppressed=true and respond with confirmation.
If HELP → respond with help message and support contact.
If START → reactivate SMS (after prior STOP).
Register webhook in Twilio console as the SMS URL for your phone number.
Register delivery status webhook separately — track deliveries in alert_sends.external_status.
Complete A2P 10DLC registration (required for US SMS, ~$4/mo + vetting).
files_affected: MODIFY: lib/sms-alerts.ts — check suppression before sending
items.sql:
alter table profiles add column if not exists sms_suppressed boolean not null default false;
alter table profiles add column if not exists sms_suppressed_at timestamptz;
verification: Text STOP from a verified number — confirm profile flagged and reply received.
Attempt to send SMS to suppressed profile — confirm skipped with log.

items.title: Stripe webhook hardening: idempotency + replay-safe
items.problem: Stripe webhooks can be delivered multiple times. If you upgrade a user's plan twice or charge them twice on a single event = refund + churn. Signature must always be verified.
solution_steps: Verify stripe-signature header on every request (you should already be doing this — double-check).
Create stripe_webhook_events table. Before processing, insert event.id with on-conflict-do-nothing. If conflict → already processed, return 200 immediately.
Process only after successful insert.
Log every event regardless of type for audit.
Return 200 OK only after state committed. Return 500 on failure so Stripe retries.
verification: Replay a Stripe event manually via CLI — confirm second delivery is no-op.
Invalid signature — confirm 401.

items.title: Global timeout + retry policy for all outbound HTTP
items.problem: Inconsistent timeouts across the codebase (Cook County is 30s, others are default 5min). A slow external call can tie up a function until Vercel kills it.
solution_steps: Create lib/http-client.ts: default 15s timeout, 2 retries with jitter for idempotent GET, 0 retries for POST unless explicitly opted in.
Use AbortController for cancellation.
Replace all bare fetch() with this helper in external API calls.
Log every outbound request duration to cron_runs (phase='external_http').
verification: Mock a hanging endpoint — confirm request aborts at 15s, not 5min.

categories.title: Security, Auth, Rate Limiting & Abuse Protection
categories.summary: At scale, you become a target. Bots, scrapers, and abuse attempts against auth and address search will be constant. You must rate-limit and harden all public endpoints.

items.title: Rate limit magic link auth endpoint
items.problem: Supabase magic link endpoint can be hit repeatedly to spam users' inboxes or probe for registered emails. Default Supabase rate limits are permissive.
solution_steps: Front the /login (or magic-link request) route with Upstash Ratelimit middleware: 3 requests per 10 min per IP, 5 per hour per email.
Return 429 with Retry-After header.
Log rate-limit hits to compliance_events for abuse monitoring.
files_affected: MODIFY: app/login/actions.ts if magic link sent server-side
verification: Hit login endpoint 10 times in 1 minute from same IP — confirm 429 from 4th request.
Monitor logs — confirm rate limit events recorded.

items.title: Rate limit address search and other public endpoints
items.problem: /api/address-search hits Socrata/Carto without auth (needed for onboarding). Scrapers can use it to mirror city databases via your quota.
solution_steps: Rate limit by IP: 30 searches per minute, 500 per day.
Rate limit by user (if authenticated): 200 per day.
Apply same to /api/analytics (anyone can POST events) — 100/min/IP.
Also apply to onboarding property-add: max 10 properties/user/day (prevents abuse + surprise costs).
verification: Script that hits address-search 100 times from one IP — confirm rate limited.
Legit onboarding flow still works.

items.title: Full RLS audit at scale
items.problem: RLS was verified for user-owned tables. But at scale, any gap = massive data leak. A single bad policy on failed_alerts, alert_sends, cron_runs, property_stats, compliance_score_history could expose everyone's data.
solution_steps: List every table: run select tablename, rowsecurity from pg_tables where schemaname='public'. Confirm rowsecurity=true on ALL user-scoped tables.
For each table, document: policies, service role access, anon access.
Use Supabase Advisors > Security — resolve every warning.
Add RLS policies to newly created tables (failed_alerts, alert_sends, cron_runs, stripe_webhook_events, email_suppressions).
Write automated test: create two users, verify User B cannot see any of User A's data via Supabase client (anon+authenticated).
Add to CI: linter check that every table in migrations has 'enable row level security' or an explicit 'disable_rls' comment.
verification: Run automated RLS test: User B attempts SELECT from every table while authenticated — zero rows of User A data returned.
CI check passes.

items.title: Service role key usage audit + rotation policy
items.problem: Service role key bypasses RLS. If it leaks = full database read/write. Every usage must be scoped and logged.
solution_steps: Grep codebase: rg 'createClient.*SERVICE_ROLE' — confirm every use is server-only (never in client code or public API routes without auth guard).
Ensure lib/supabase/admin.ts is ONLY imported from /app/api/cron/*, /lib/inngest/*, and admin-only server actions.
Rotate service role key quarterly via Supabase dashboard.
Document rotation procedure in runbook.
Consider Supabase JWT with custom scopes for less-privileged admin operations (future).
verification: grep output shows zero admin client imports in client components.
Key rotation tested in staging.

items.title: Add security headers and CSP
items.problem: Missing headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options) leave you vulnerable to clickjacking, XSS, downgrade attacks. Browsers increasingly penalize missing CSP in SEO.
solution_steps: Add next.config.js headers: Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options=DENY, X-Content-Type-Options=nosniff, Referrer-Policy=strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy.

Add Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://js.stripe.com; frame-src https://js.stripe.com; connect-src 'self' https://*.supabase.co; img-src 'self' data:;
Test every page — adjust CSP until no blocked resources.
Validate with securityheaders.com — target A+ grade.
verification: curl -I casalerts.com | grep -i 'strict-transport\|content-security' — confirms present.
securityheaders.com scan returns A+.

items.title: CSRF protection verification on all server actions
items.problem: Next.js 14 server actions default to same-origin only, but if any action is exposed via custom API route or accepts cross-origin, CSRF is possible.
solution_steps: Verify all mutations go through server actions (not custom POST routes without CSRF).
For any custom POST route (e.g. webhooks), verify origin or signature.
Reject any mutation from Origin !== casalerts.com unless explicitly allowlisted.
verification: Attempt cross-origin POST to server action — confirm 403.

items.title: PII minimization and encryption at rest review
items.problem: You collect email, phone, property addresses, resolution data (may include contractor contact info). Supabase encrypts at rest via AWS. But you need to verify and document for future SOC 2 / enterprise sales.
solution_steps: Confirm Supabase tier includes at-rest encryption (Pro does).
Review what fields truly need to be stored — drop any that don't (e.g., do you need full phone or just last 4?).
For contractor phone numbers in resolutions: consider hashing or partial storage.
Document retention policy: inactive accounts deleted after 12 months of inactivity (or per user GDPR request).
Add profiles.deletion_requested_at and background worker to process.
verification: Submit deletion request via UI — confirm full cascade deletion within 30 days.

items.title: WAF / bot protection at the edge
items.problem: Scrapers, credential stuffing, and DDoS attempts increase with traffic. Vercel provides basic DDoS but not full WAF.
solution_steps: Option A (simplest): Enable Vercel Pro Web Application Firewall (~$10/mo).
Option B: Front with Cloudflare (free tier) — bot management, WAF rules, caching.
Configure rules: block known-bad bot signatures, challenge suspicious patterns, geo-restrict admin routes to your IPs.
Monitor Vercel/Cloudflare logs weekly for anomalies.
verification: Attempt common scan patterns (sqlmap signatures) — confirm blocked.
Load test continues to work at legitimate volumes.

categories.title: Input Validation & Error Handling
categories.summary: Every server action and API route must validate inputs before touching the database. Currently inconsistent — some routes trust client data.

items.title: Zod schemas on every server action and API route
items.problem: Untrusted input reaching DB/enrichment logic can cause crashes, data corruption, or security issues. Even a stray null or oversized string can break downstream.
solution_steps: Add zod package (if not present).
Create lib/schemas/ directory with one file per entity: property.ts, resolution.ts, profile.ts, questionnaire.ts, reminder.ts.
In each server action (app/**/actions.ts) and API route: parse input with schema.parse() at top, return typed error on validation failure.
Client forms should use matching schemas via react-hook-form + @hookform/resolvers/zod.
Define strict bounds: address max 200 chars, nickname max 80, cost max 500000, phone E.164 format, email RFC-compliant.
files_affected: NEW: lib/schemas/property.ts, lib/schemas/resolution.ts, lib/schemas/profile.ts, lib/schemas/questionnaire.ts, lib/schemas/reminder.ts
verification: Unit test each schema with valid + invalid inputs.
Attempt POST with oversized address (1000 chars) — confirm 400.
Attempt negative cost — confirm 400.

items.title: Address normalization before lookup
items.problem: '1234 W Madison' and '1234 w madison st' and '1234 WEST MADISON' refer to same property but match differently against city APIs. Silent data duplication.
solution_steps: Create lib/address-normalizer.ts: uppercase, strip periods, standardize direction abbreviations (N/S/E/W), strip suffix variations (St/Street, Ave/Avenue).
Apply in onboarding before fetching violations.
Store normalized_address column on properties.
Add unique constraint on (user_id, normalized_address) to prevent duplicates.
items.sql:
alter table properties add column if not exists normalized_address text;
create unique index if not exists ux_properties_user_normalized_address on properties(user_id, normalized_address) where normalized_address is not null;
verification: Onboard '1234 W Madison' then '1234 west madison st' — second should detect duplicate.

items.title: Standardized API error response shape
items.problem: Different routes return errors in different shapes. Client code cannot uniformly handle them.
solution_steps: Define: { ok: false, error: { code: string, message: string, details?: any } }.
Define: { ok: true, data: T }.
Create lib/api-response.ts with apiOk / apiErr helpers.
Migrate all API routes to this shape.
verification: Every API route returns consistent shape.

categories.title: Observability, Monitoring & Alerting
categories.summary: You cannot manage what you cannot measure. At 100k users, silent failures become expensive. Invest in visibility now.

items.title: Install Sentry for runtime error tracking
items.problem: Unhandled exceptions currently go to console.error — lost unless you're watching Vercel logs. A single null reference in a hot path could affect thousands of users before you notice.
solution_steps: Sign up for Sentry free tier (5k events/month). Upgrade to Team ($26/mo) at 50k users.
Install @sentry/nextjs, run wizard.
Configure sentry.client.config.ts, sentry.server.config.ts, sentry.edge.config.ts.
Set tracesSampleRate: 0.1 (sample 10% traces to control cost), errorsSampleRate: 1.0.
Tag every scope with user.id (from Supabase auth) for correlation.
Mask PII: filter out email/phone from breadcrumbs.
Configure Slack/email alerts for new error types, error rate spikes.
verification: Throw a test error — confirm shows in Sentry dashboard within 30s.
Verify PII not leaked in Sentry event.

items.title: Structured JSON logging with correlation IDs
items.problem: console.log scattered across codebase — no structure, no way to filter or join logs for a given user action spanning multiple functions.
solution_steps: Create lib/logger.ts using pino (fast, JSON-native).
Every log includes: timestamp, level, msg, requestId, userId, route, duration_ms.
Generate requestId in middleware.ts (random UUID) — pass via AsyncLocalStorage or via header to downstream.
Replace all console.log in lib/ and app/api/ with logger.info / logger.error.
Ship to Vercel Log Drains → Axiom or Datadog (free/cheap tier) for searchable logs.
files_affected: MODIFY: every file using console.log in lib/ and app/api/
verification: A single user action generates logs with consistent requestId across multiple functions.
Can search Axiom for 'userId=X' and see full session trace.

items.title: Uptime monitoring (BetterStack / UptimeRobot)
items.problem: If casalerts.com goes down or CRON stops, you need to know in minutes, not hours.
solution_steps: BetterStack free tier: 10 monitors, 3-min interval.
Monitor: homepage (GET /, expect 200), app login (GET /login, 200), CRON health (GET /api/health/cron, 200), webhook endpoints.
Alert via SMS + email to founder cell on any failure >2 intervals.
Public status page at status.casalerts.com (BetterStack auto-generates).
verification: Take staging offline — alert fires in <6 min.

items.title: Business metrics dashboard (signup funnel, alert volume, CRON health)
items.problem: You cannot run a SaaS without visibility into: daily signups, daily paid conversions, MRR, churn, alerts sent, CRON success rate, data freshness SLO.
solution_steps: Build app/admin/dashboard/page.tsx (protected by admin role).
Show: 7-day signups chart, 7-day paid conversions, current MRR, 24h alerts sent, last CRON run status, % properties scanned in last 25h (freshness SLO), failed_alerts count, open violations per tier.
Use read replica (db-06) for these queries.
Optional: ship to PostHog or Mixpanel for richer analytics.
verification: Dashboard loads in <2s.
Numbers match manual SQL queries against DB.

items.title: Anomaly detection on alert volume
items.problem: If CRON runs but produces 0 alerts for 24h, that's broken (very likely a bug in classification or scanning). Without automated anomaly detection you might not notice for a week.
solution_steps: Add hourly Inngest cron: query alert_sends count for last hour.
Compare to 7-day rolling average for same hour-of-day.
If < 20% of average → fire Sentry alert + email founder.
Similarly: alert if error rate in sentry exceeds 1% of requests.
verification: Seed scenario with 0 alerts — confirm anomaly alert fires.

items.title: Vercel deployment notifications
items.problem: Failed or unexpected deploys go unnoticed. A bad deploy at 2am ruins the next day.
solution_steps: Vercel Settings > Integrations > Slack (or email).
Notify on: deploy started, deploy succeeded, deploy failed.
Also notify on preview deploys if you merge frequently.
verification: Trigger a deploy — confirm Slack/email notification.

categories.title: Data Integrity Checks & Auto-Remediation
categories.summary: Your competitive moat is the data. Silent corruption or missing fields destroy that moat. Active checks + auto-remediation.

items.title: Weekly data integrity check job
items.problem: Without active monitoring, you discover data issues weeks or months later when analytics queries fail or users complain.
solution_steps: Create lib/inngest/functions/data-integrity-check.ts running weekly (Sundays 3am UTC).

Checks: violations with null severity, properties with null zip/lat/lng where expected, resolutions with null violation_external_id, orphaned rows (violations referencing deleted properties), compliance_score_history gaps (>2 day skips per property), property_stats staleness (>24h old).
For each issue found: email founder + insert into data_integrity_issues table for tracking.
Auto-remediate what's safe: backfill severity using lib/compliance-score.getViolationSeverity(); trigger re-enrich for missing geo.
items.sql:
create table data_integrity_issues (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  check_name text not null,
  entity_type text not null,
  entity_id uuid,
  details jsonb,
  detected_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  remediated_at timestamptz,
  remediation_type text
);
create index idx_data_integrity_open on data_integrity_issues(check_name) where remediated_at is null;
verification: Manually null a severity column — run check — confirm issue logged and auto-remediated within the same run.

items.title: Trigger-based severity backfill at insert
items.problem: Even with NOT NULL constraint, if a code path forgets to set severity, insert fails. Better to auto-classify at DB level if missing.
solution_steps: Create severity classification function in plpgsql mirroring lib/compliance-score.getViolationSeverity.
BEFORE INSERT trigger: if severity_classification is null, call classifier.
Keep application-level code setting explicitly as primary — trigger is backup.
Document: must update both Postgres function AND TypeScript function when keyword list changes.
verification: Manually insert violation with severity=null — confirm classified correctly by trigger.

items.title: Resolution data preservation audit
items.problem: The most valuable data is resolutions (cost, contractor, rating). A rescan where external_id changes could orphan resolutions. A cascading delete could wipe them silently.
solution_steps: Audit all FOREIGN KEY constraints on violation_resolutions. Confirm on-delete behavior: violation_id -> SET NULL (not CASCADE), property_id -> SET NULL, user_id -> CASCADE only if user account deleted.
Create backup trigger: on delete from violations or properties, copy any linked resolutions to archived_resolutions.
Weekly check: count resolutions with both violation_id=null AND violation_external_id=null — these are unlinked and bad. Alert immediately.
verification: Delete a violation with a resolution — confirm resolution archived.
Audit FKs: select conname, confdeltype from pg_constraint where conrelid='violation_resolutions'::regclass;

categories.title: Backups & Disaster Recovery
categories.summary: Assume everything will eventually fail. You need recovery paths tested before disaster, not during.

items.title: Enable Supabase PITR + verify daily backups
items.problem: Pro plan includes daily backups but you must verify they're enabled and working. PITR (Point-In-Time Recovery) is an add-on that lets you restore to any second in the last 7 days.
solution_steps: Supabase Dashboard > Project > Database > Backups. Confirm daily backups running (view last 7 days).
Enable PITR add-on (~$100/mo, recommended at 20k+ users).
Document recovery SLAs: RPO (recovery point) = 24h without PITR, 1 min with PITR. RTO (recovery time) = 2-4h to restore.
verification: View 7 consecutive daily backup rows in Supabase dashboard.
Open a support ticket with Supabase to simulate PITR restore (they can guide test).

items.title: Weekly off-site pg_dump to S3
items.problem: Supabase controls its own backups. If Supabase has an incident, you want an independent copy you control.
solution_steps: GitHub Actions workflow: weekly pg_dump of production DB, encrypt, upload to AWS S3 (or Cloudflare R2 — cheaper).
Retention: keep last 12 weekly dumps.
Encrypt with GPG using a key stored in 1Password (not in repo).
Test restore of a weekly dump to a fresh Supabase project quarterly.
verification: First run completes and uploads ~100MB file to S3.
Quarterly test restore succeeds.

items.title: Document + test full disaster recovery runbook
items.problem: In an incident you don't want to be googling 'how to restore Postgres'. Need step-by-step runbook tested before crisis.
solution_steps: Document scenarios: total DB loss, accidental DROP TABLE, corrupted migration, Supabase region outage.
For each: recovery steps, estimated time, communication plan.
Schedule game day: each quarter, pick a scenario and run through it end-to-end in staging.
Keep runbook in docs/runbooks/ in repo (version controlled).
verification: First game day completes successfully — staging restored to known-good state.

categories.title: Testing, CI/CD & Deployment Safety
categories.summary: Every deploy at 100k users is a potential outage. Invest in automated safety.

items.title: Set up staging environment with separate Supabase project
items.problem: Testing migrations and code changes against production data is reckless. One bad migration = corrupted data for 100k users.
solution_steps: Create second Supabase project (staging): Free tier works for low-traffic testing.
Mirror schema via Supabase CLI: supabase db dump -> supabase db reset in staging.
Seed staging with anonymized production-scale data (see test-02).
Vercel: configure Preview deployments to use staging Supabase env vars.
All migrations run in staging first for 24h before production.
files_affected: MODIFY: Vercel env vars (add staging branch)
verification: Deploy a PR to preview — hits staging DB, not production.
Migration runs successfully in staging.

items.title: Seed script for realistic staging data at scale
items.problem: Testing at 10 records doesn't expose query performance issues. You need staging seeded with 100k-scale data.
solution_steps: scripts/seed-staging.ts: generate 10k test users, 30k properties, 100k violations, 10k resolutions with realistic distributions.
Use faker.js for realistic names/addresses. Anonymize any production samples.
Never copy production PII to staging.
Run seed after each staging reset.
verification: After seed: staging has expected row counts. Dashboard loads realistically.

items.title: Unit tests for critical lib functions
items.problem: Compliance score, severity classification, and risk briefing are the core IP. A regression here = silently wrong data across entire platform.
solution_steps: Install vitest.
Test first: lib/compliance-score.ts (getViolationSeverity, calculateComplianceScore) — 30+ test cases covering all severity keywords.
Test: lib/compliance-events.ts, lib/risk-briefing.ts, lib/property-enrichment.ts (with mocked HTTP).
Test: lib/alert-idempotency.ts.
Target >80% coverage on lib/.
Run on every PR.
verification: npm test — all pass.
Coverage report shows >80% on lib/.

items.title: Playwright E2E tests for critical flows
items.problem: Onboarding, resolution submission, and billing are the revenue-critical flows. Regressions = lost revenue.
solution_steps: Install @playwright/test.
Tests: signup via magic link (use mailosaur), onboarding happy path, resolution submission with all fields, Stripe checkout (test mode), settings changes.
Run against staging on every PR.
Include a smoke test that runs post-production-deploy.
verification: All E2E tests pass in staging.

items.title: GitHub Actions CI pipeline
items.problem: Without CI, bad code reaches production.
solution_steps: Workflow on PR: lint (eslint), type-check (tsc --noEmit), unit tests (vitest), migration lint (check RLS on new tables).
Workflow on merge to main: full E2E against staging, then auto-deploy preview, wait for manual promote to production.
Block merges with failing checks.
verification: Submit PR with type error — blocked.
Pass checks — merge allowed, deploys to preview.

items.title: Database migration workflow (Supabase CLI)
items.problem: Editing schema via Supabase dashboard means your schema is not in version control. At scale this is chaos.
solution_steps: All schema changes via supabase migration new <name> + supabase db push.
Migrations committed to repo under supabase/migrations/.
Never edit Supabase dashboard schema directly in production — always PR + migration.
Document migration review checklist: RLS on new tables, indexes on new columns, reversible, tested in staging first.
verification: All future schema changes in migrations only.

items.title: Feature flags (PostHog or Vercel Edge Config)
items.problem: Rolling out risky features all-at-once at 100k users is dangerous. Need ability to gradually enable or kill features without deploy.
solution_steps: Integrate PostHog feature flags (free tier covers this).
Wrap risky new features: if (await flagEnabled('alert_mode_daily_digest', userId)) { ... }.
Rollout: 1% → 10% → 50% → 100% with monitoring in between.
Kill switch: flip to 0% instantly on issue.
verification: Flag enabled for specific user, disabled for others.

categories.title: Legal & Regulatory Compliance
categories.summary: As a UK Ltd with US users and US data, you have GDPR, CCPA, CAN-SPAM, CASL, and CTIA obligations. Non-compliance at scale = fines + enterprise deals blocked.

items.title: GDPR data export flow
items.problem: GDPR Article 15 requires data export within 30 days of request. CCPA similar. Must be automated at scale.
solution_steps: Settings page: 'Export my data' button.
Fires server action that assembles JSON of: profile, all properties, all violations, all resolutions, all compliance events, all analytics events.
Sends via email as ZIP within 10 minutes.
Log request + completion in compliance_events type='data_export_requested/completed'.
verification: Request export — receive ZIP with all records within 10 min.

items.title: GDPR account deletion flow
items.problem: GDPR Article 17 (right to erasure). Must delete all PII within 30 days. But you want to retain aggregated/anonymized data for analytics.
solution_steps: Settings: 'Delete my account' button, double confirm.
Marks profile.deletion_requested_at = now().

Inngest daily job processes: anonymize profile (email→sha256, phone→null, name→null), delete properties (cascades to violations, resolutions), keep aggregated compliance_events with user_id set to null.
Email user when complete.
Retain anonymized resolution cost data for moat — removing PII but keeping 'a resolution happened for $X in this category in Chicago in April 2026'.
verification: Request deletion — after 24h, profile anonymized, data queryable shows no PII.

items.title: Updated Privacy Policy + Terms of Service covering all data collection
items.problem: Given the amount of data you collect (resolutions, behavioral signals, contractor info), your privacy policy must clearly disclose it. Vague language = GDPR violations.
solution_steps: Work with a lawyer (use iubenda or Termly for templates, then lawyer review).
Disclose every data point collected, purpose, retention, sharing.
Specific language around resolution data being aggregated for market intelligence products (future revenue).
ToS covers: service uptime, user obligations, payment terms, dispute resolution, limitation of liability.
Cookie banner if EU users (cookie consent management).
verification: Legal review complete.
Policies cover every field in database.

items.title: SMS A2P 10DLC registration
items.problem: US SMS regulations require Application-to-Person registration. Without it, carriers block your messages. Also fines from CTIA.
solution_steps: Twilio Console > Messaging > A2P 10DLC Registration.
Register as sole proprietor or small business (CasAlerts Ltd).
Submit use case: 'Customer service notifications for housing code violations.'
Wait for vetting (1-4 weeks).
Register your brand + campaign.
verification: Twilio dashboard shows campaign status = approved.
Test SMS delivers successfully.

items.title: CAN-SPAM + CASL email compliance
items.problem: Every marketing/transactional email must: include physical address, provide unsubscribe, not deceive in subject. Non-compliance = $50k/email fines.
solution_steps: Audit all Resend templates in lib/email-alerts.ts — verify footer includes: business name, UK registered address, unsubscribe link.
Build /unsubscribe page that accepts token-signed URL: toggles email preferences without requiring login.
Subject lines must not deceive.
verification: Every email contains all required elements.
Unsubscribe link works and disables future sends.

items.title: Data Processing Agreement with sub-processors
items.problem: For GDPR and enterprise sales: formal DPAs with Supabase, Resend, Twilio, Stripe, Vercel, Inngest.
solution_steps: Each provider has a standard DPA — sign them via their compliance portals.
Maintain list of sub-processors at casalerts.com/subprocessors.
Notify users 30 days before adding new sub-processors (in ToS).
verification: All DPAs signed and stored.

categories.title: Cost Controls & Infrastructure Hygiene
categories.summary: At scale, small inefficiencies become big bills.

items.title: Analytics events TTL (180-day retention for raw)
items.problem: Raw analytics_events at 100M+ rows/year will dominate storage cost. Most insights don't need raw events past 6 months.
solution_steps: Aggregate daily: run nightly job that computes daily metric rollups into analytics_daily table.
Drop partitions > 180 days old (db-02 makes this trivial).
Keep rollups indefinitely (tiny).
verification: Partition older than 180 days dropped.
Historical trends still queryable from rollup.

items.title: Compliance score history: aggregate > 2 years
items.problem: Daily snapshots per property for years = 100M+ rows. Users only need recent granularity — older data fine as weekly.
solution_steps: After 2 years, collapse daily → weekly averages.
Keep monthly averages indefinitely for trend analysis.
verification: Run on test data — 730 rows collapsed to ~100 weekly averages.

items.title: Resend + Twilio volume plan review
items.problem: Pay-as-you-go pricing is expensive at volume. Volume plans cut costs 40-60%.
solution_steps: At 50k emails/mo: Resend Pro $90.
At 100k+ emails/mo: Resend Growth.
Twilio: evaluate short code (higher throughput, better deliverability, ~$1k/mo) at 100k+ SMS/mo.
Monitor monthly spend — set budget alerts.
verification: Monthly spend tracked in founder dashboard.

items.title: Supabase storage monitoring
items.problem: DB storage overage is $0.125/GB. Easy to miss.
solution_steps: Enable Supabase usage alerts (Settings > Billing > Usage Alerts).
Alert at 75% of included storage.
Monthly review of largest tables: select relname, pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(oid)) from pg_class order by pg_total_relation_size(oid) desc limit 20.
verification: Alert configured and received during testing.

items.title: Vercel bandwidth monitoring + CDN optimization
items.problem: Bandwidth overages at $0.40/GB above included tier add up with image-heavy emails and dashboards.
solution_steps: Audit next/image usage — all images served optimized.
Static assets cached with long max-age.
Review Vercel Analytics weekly for anomalies.
verification: Monthly bandwidth trend stays flat with user growth.

items.title: React Suspense + streaming for dashboard
items.problem: Dashboard currently waits for all queries before rendering. Slow networks see blank screen for seconds.
solution_steps: Wrap slow data fetches in Suspense boundaries.
Render shell immediately, stream property cards as data arrives.
Use loading.tsx per route.
Use React Server Components where possible to avoid client bundle cost.
verification: Lighthouse score >90 for performance.
TTFB < 200ms, LCP < 2s.

items.title: Bundle size audit
items.problem: Next.js bundles can bloat from dependencies. Every KB slows mobile.
solution_steps: Run @next/bundle-analyzer. Identify largest deps.
Replace heavy libs with lighter alternatives (e.g., date-fns over moment).
Dynamic import for non-critical components (charts, admin panels).
Target: main bundle <150KB gzipped.
verification: Bundle analyzer report shows no single dep >50KB.
First-load JS <150KB on dashboard.

items.title: Image optimization
items.problem: Email images and dashboard assets could be unoptimized.
solution_steps: All replaced with next/image where possible.
Email images hosted on CDN, sized correctly, WebP.
Property thumbnails lazy-loaded.
verification: Lighthouse image score perfect.

categories.title: Load Testing Before Scaling
categories.summary: Find bottlenecks in staging, not in production.

items.title: k6 load tests on critical paths
items.problem: You don't know where the next bottleneck is until you simulate load. Better in staging than production.
solution_steps: Install k6.
Scripts: 1000 concurrent dashboard page views, 500 concurrent onboarding flows, 200 concurrent resolution submissions.
Run against fully-seeded staging (test-02).
Target: p95 TTFB <500ms under 1000 concurrent. Error rate <0.1%.
Identify bottleneck. Fix. Repeat.
verification: All critical paths pass SLA in k6 run.

items.title: Simulate full-scale CRON in staging
items.problem: CRON with 210k properties has different failure modes than 1k. Must simulate at scale.
solution_steps: Seed staging with 210k properties.
Run full CRON end-to-end.
Measure: total duration, error rate, DB connection pool pressure, worker concurrency limits.
Tune concurrency, batch sizes, retries until run completes cleanly in <1h.
verification: Full-scale CRON in staging completes successfully.

categories.title: Incident Response
categories.summary: When things break, having a plan matters more than never breaking.

items.title: Incident response runbook
items.problem: Without a plan, incidents take 3x longer to resolve and communication is chaotic.
solution_steps: Document: severity levels (SEV1/SEV2/SEV3), criteria, on-call contact, communication channels, escalation.
SEV1 (down/data loss): <30 min response. Page founder. Status page update.
SEV2 (degraded): <2h response. Slack alert.
SEV3 (minor): next business day.
Template: incident log, RCA doc, customer comms.
verification: Runbook reviewed and rehearsed.

items.title: Public status page
items.problem: When users experience issues, they check for a status page. Absence signals amateur hour.
solution_steps: BetterStack Status Page (free, bundled with uptime).
Custom domain: status.casalerts.com.
Auto-updates from uptime monitors.
Manual incident posting for outages you discover first.
verification: status.casalerts.com loads with current status.

items.title: Postmortem template + process
items.problem: Without postmortems, same mistakes repeat.
solution_steps: Template: what happened, timeline, root cause, customer impact, action items with owners.
Required for every SEV1 and SEV2.
Stored in docs/postmortems/. Review quarterly for patterns.
Blameless culture — focus on system, not people.
verification: First incident produces completed postmortem.
